gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS P1800's own solar port is limited to 11–60 V and 13 A (650 W ceiling), or that ALLPOWERS sells a P1800 kit with a 600 W panel ($798) that stays under that ceiling. That kit refills faster than the 400 W kit ChatGPT picked, as long as the 600 W panel works at 46 V or more so 13 A is enough.
standout_why: Trek4Tech (cited) gives only wattage ceilings: C1000 600 W, AC180 500 W, Explorer 1000 v2 400 W, Delta 2 500 W, Explorer 2000 v2 400 W and River 2 Pro 220 W. It names no voltage or amp window and doesn't cover the P1800. It only says to check that 'the voltage, current and wiring fit'. ChatGPT's answer gives the same ~3.4–4.3 h for all three 400 W kits, with no input limits and no 600 W option. I could not read TheOutagePlan (cited) because of a TLS certificate error, so it is not compared.
decides: This changes the pick inside the same product line. ChatGPT chose the P1800 + 400 W kit. ALLPOWERS's US store also sells a P1800 + 600 W kit for $798, $100 more, and the P1800's 650 W XT60 input can take all 600 W. On the maker's ratings, that is 1,024 Wh against 600 W instead of 400 W, about 1.7 h at full rating instead of 2.6 h, before losses. Whether the panel really delivers 600 W depends on its operating voltage, because the input caps current at 13 A. At 13 A the port reaches 600 W only from about 46.2 V up (600 ÷ 13). The same cap limits the 400 W SP037: at its 37.4 V figure it can reach about 486 W, enough for 400 W. EcoFlow's '70-minute' DELTA 3 Plus claim needs 2 × 500 W inputs (1,000 W). EcoFlow's US store doesn't list a 400 W DELTA 3 Plus bundle (160 W, 220 W, 2 × 220 W only), so ChatGPT's EcoFlow card isn't a US maker kit. BLUETTI caps the AC180 at 500 W, so its 2 × 200 W kit gets nothing from the extra input room.
